summary: Hermann Jacobi was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Albrecht Weber and the University of Bonn under Johann Gildemeister. He held professorships at Münster (1876–1885), Kiel (1885), Bonn (1889–1922), and also taught in Cologne.

Hermann Kulke was a historian and Indologist who studied at the University of Freiburg under Hermann Goetz, the University of Madras, and Heidelberg University. He held academic posts at Heidelberg (1967–1988) and served as Chair of Asian History at Kiel University (1988–2003).

Hermann Oldenberg worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Göttingen and Humboldt University of Berlin, later holding professorships at Humboldt University of Berlin (1878), Kiel University (1889–1908), and the University of Göttingen (1908).

Hermann Olshausen was a religious studies scholar who studied at Kiel University and Humboldt University of Berlin. He held academic posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1820–1821), the University of Königsberg (1827–1834), and the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1834–1839).

Hermann Osthoff worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Berlin, Tübingen, Bonn under Hermann Usener, and Leipzig under Georg Curtius. He held posts at Leipzig (~1875–1877) and served as ordinarius at Heidelberg University from 1877.

Hermann Sauppe was a scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology who earned his doctorate at the University of Leipzig under Gottfried Hermann. He served as Privatdozent at the University of Zurich (1833) and later as professor at the University of Göttingen (1855).
Hermann Schlagintweit studied at the University of Munich from ~1845 to 1849 and held a post at Humboldt University of Berlin from ~1851 to 1854.

Hermann Usener was a religious studies scholar who studied at Heidelberg, Munich, Göttingen, and Bonn. He held academic posts at the University of Bern (~1861–1863), the University of Greifswald (~1863–1866), and the University of Bonn (~1866–1905).

Hermann Wilhelm Ebel was a linguist who studied at Halle-Wittenberg and Humboldt University of Berlin under August Boeckh, August Friedrich Pott, and Franz Bopp. He held teaching posts at school level before succeeding Bopp as chair of comparative philology in Berlin (1872).

Hew McLeod was a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at Nelson College, the University of Otago (~1950–1954), and SOAS University of London (~1962–1965), later holding a post at the University of Otago (~1971–1997).

Heymann Steinthal worked in linguistics and philosophy, studying under August Boeckh at Humboldt University of Berlin. He held posts at Humboldt University of Berlin / Frederick William University (~1850–1899) and the Hochschule für die Wissenschaft des Judentums (~1872–1899).
Hideaki Kimura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Taisho University and held a researcher post there (attested 1995).

Hideaki Nakatani is an Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University under Gadjin Nagao and Yutaka Ochihara, and earned a PhD at Sorbonne Nouvelle University. He was attested as a professor at Kobe Gakuin University in 2003.
Hidehiko Kurita is a scholar of religious studies and Japanology who completed a PhD at Tohoku University and was attested as a lecturer at Aichi Prefectural University in 2020.
Hideki Kiyoshima works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Delhi and was attested as a lecturer at Kindai University in 1989.
Hidemasa Nagata was a historian and Sinologist who studied at Kyoto University from ~1952 to 1961 and held an academic post there from ~1974 to 1997.

Hidenaka Tanaka was a linguist who studied at the University of Tokyo under Raphael von Koeber, the University of Oxford, and Kyoto University. He taught at Tokyo, served as assistant professor at Kyoto University (1931–1946), and was a professor at Kyoto Women's University (~1954–1974).

Hidenori Kitagawa was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Hakuju Ui. He was a Rockefeller Foundation fellow (1952–1953) and served as a professor at Nagoya University (attested 1968–1969).

Hidenori S. Sakuma is a Buddhist studies scholar, Indologist, and Tibetologist who studied at Tokyo and completed his PhD under Lambert Schmithausen at Hamburg. He held professorships at Shitennoji University (attested 1991–1998) and the University of Tsukuba (attested 2003–2011).

Hideo Mineshima was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Taisho University and Waseda University. He was a lecturer, assistant professor, and professor at Waseda University (1960–1998), and later served as a professor at Bunkyo Gakuin University.
